summary: A community-managed Doi Inthanon walk follows forest streams and Pha Dok Siew waterfall down to Ban Mae Klang Luang, where village-grown coffee and mountain scenery make a satisfying finish. The Karen community provides guides; treat the waterfall flow and December 2026 operating status as weather dependent.
whyGo: Combine a forest hike, waterfall crossings, mountain scenery and a village stop in one outing.
A local guide supports the community and can interpret the landscape along the route.
bestFor: Active travellers who want a more intimate Doi Inthanon day than roadside viewpoints alone.
Hikers comfortable with uneven ground, steps and a one-way route.
skipIf: You need wheelchair access or have difficulty with steep steps and slippery natural surfaces.
A strong waterfall or green rice terraces are essential: December flow and field conditions vary.
duration: Allow about 2–3 hours for the 5.3 km trail, plus roughly two hours each way by road from Chiang Mai; reserve most of a day. Route time is a planning estimate and varies with stops and pace.
cost: A Doi Inthanon guide source reports THB 220 for one person or THB 300 for two; confirm the current community guide charge locally. Park admission and transport are extra. A recent park guide lists foreign adult admission at THB 300, but the 2026 tariff is unconfirmed.
hours: Daylight hiking only; no reliable official daily opening or last-start time was found. Confirm trail and guide availability with the park or local operator shortly before travel, especially after heavy rain.
bestTime: December is in the cool, usually drier season and often brings comfortable walking weather. Go in the morning for more time and daylight. Waterfall volume reflects recent rainfall, while rice terraces may be harvested or less green by December.
gettingThere: The trail is in Doi Inthanon National Park, around two hours by road from Chiang Mai. Use a private driver, rental car or tour that explicitly includes Pha Dok Siew. The route ends at Ban Mae Klang Luang, so arrange pickup there; do not assume a shuttle between trail ends.
booking: A local guide is required according to the specialist trail operator and travel sources; guides are arranged at the trailhead/community. For a self-drive day, confirm where to meet the guide and how your driver will reach the village endpoint. Day tours from Chiang Mai bundle transport and the hike.
accessibility: Not suitable for wheelchair users. The route has uneven forest paths, bamboo/wood bridges and many steps, including steep sections near the falls. Surfaces can be slippery; mobility and balance are needed.
practicalTips: Wear shoes with reliable grip and carry water, a light rain layer and cash for the guide and village purchases.
Ask about trail condition and water level after rain; follow the guide’s advice around streams and falls and do not swim unless explicitly permitted.
Agree on your village-end pickup before starting; add time for coffee or lunch in Mae Klang Luang.
decemberNotes: December offers cooler walking conditions after the main rainy season, but lower stream flow is possible and cannot be inferred from the calendar alone. Rice terraces are seasonal and may have been harvested. The park’s current fee and any temporary trail closure should be checked close to the visit; holiday traffic can lengthen the Chiang Mai drive.
uncertainties: No official DNP page confirming December 2026 opening, operating hours, or current admission and guide fees was located.
Guide pricing differs by party size and source; ask the community guide directly for the current rate.
Waterfall flow, trail condition and terrace appearance depend on recent weather and agricultural timing.
